newsitem.title: CANADA: Plant problems cut NOVA chemical earnings.
newsitem.headline: Plant problems cut NOVA chemical earnings.

text.p: Canadian chemical and pipeline concern NOVA Corp said on Tuesday that operational problems at one of its plants and and a drop in polyethylene sales volumes combined to cut its chemical division's second-quarter operating profits.

NOVA said operating income at its Sarnia, Ontario facility was reduced by about C$11 million during the quarter because of a series of manufacturing problems, including a turbine failure at its partially owned power generation plant.
Also, a "return to more normal sales levels" for polyethylene after a record first quarter was reflected in the April-June 1997 results, the company said.
NOVA on Tuesday reported company-wide net income of C$120 million or C$0.26 a share in the second quarter, up from C$103 million or C$0.22 a share in the same period last year.
Revenues totalled C$1.16 billion, up from C$1.13 billion last year.
NOVA Chemicals' net income was C$57 million, up from C$46 million in the second quarter of 1996 but down from C$71 million in the first quarter of this year.
During the quarter, the company implemented in North America a US3 cent a pound increase in the price of polyethylene.
The price of linear low-density polyethylene on the U.S. Gulf Coast averaged US47 cents a pound, up from US45 cents in the first quarter and US39 cents in the second quarter of 1996.
The company said styrene and polystyrene markets continued to be weak, and a sharp drop in year-over-year results in styrenics was related to low selling prices and high feedstock costs, it said.
"As a result of capacity expansions in North America and Asia, no significant improvement in market conditions is expected in the near term," NOVA said.
A bright spot during the quarter, NOVA said, was strong sales by 25-percent-owned Methanex Corp.
Meanwhile, gas pipeline unit NOVA Gas Transmission contributed C$50 million to NOVA's net earnings in the second quarter, up from C$42 million in the same period last year, the company said.
It said capital spending on the intra-Alberta pipeline system was expected to total C$460 million in 1997.
The company repeated that its pipeline system, faced with various "bypass" proposals from such groups as Alliance Pipeline, continued to be the lowest-cost option for gas transport in the province.
"We are developing new price and service options that we believe will deliver the transportation price modifications and certainty we and the shippers are seeking," NOVA said.
NOVA shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange were up 0.05 on Tuesday to 11.95 with 1.3 million shares changing hands.
The company said its lackluster stock market performance was caused by analyst concerns over future chemical prices and weakness in partially owned NGC Corp's stock price.
NOVA's share price is down three percent for 1997, underperforming the TSE 300, it said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
